key_insight: Diagonal SSM transitions commute, limiting group tracking to commutative groups; HyperSSM adds quaternion channels to capture order-sensitive structure.
engineering_relevance: HyperSSM preserves linear-time inference and parallel training while enabling compact, interpretable memory for order-dependent computations.
method: Model sequence updates as a linear representation of the input-sequence monoid.
Characterize trackable groups as quotients of the group generated by transition matrices.
Add quaternion channels alongside real and complex components.
evidence_signal: With final-answer-only training, HyperSSM exactly solves the reported group tasks using at most five state numbers, including S5 with 32 generators, and generalizes to sequences 25× longer than training sequences.
watch_item: The abstract does not establish whether these group-task gains translate to broad language-modeling or production workloads.
paper_title: Symmetry in Time: A Representation Theory of Linear Recurrent Memory
